target.title: fix(memory): recover from same-file legacy index divergence
target.body:
Related: #108532

Continues #109865. This supersedes that stalled PR because its contributor branch cannot be updated from this environment. Credit to @Serhii-Leniv for the original fix; the first three commits preserve Serhii Leniv's authorship.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with legacy and canonical Memory Core rows in the same per-agent SQLite database could enter a Gateway crash loop when rows shared an identity but held different values. In this state, `openclaw doctor --fix` could report success without repairing the database, and the next Gateway start failed again.

The original report is closed as #108532, but its [Docker reproduction and doctor evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108532#issuecomment-4987458050) show the same-file failure remained: the mounted `main.sqlite` kept conflicting after doctor ran and the Gateway still refused to start. This PR preserves that paper trail without reopening the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Summary

Same-file migration now treats existing canonical rows as authoritative, imports non-conflicting legacy-only rows, and drops the legacy tables only after proving every eligible identity is represented canonically. Chunk migration snapshots ownership before copying so stale chunks cannot be mixed into a source that already has a canonical chunk set. A partially migrated, chunkless source imports legacy chunks only when its source metadata still matches; divergent source metadata is removed so normal source sync must rebuild current content instead of accepting stale chunks.

If a canonical source has some chunks but legacy exposes additional chunk identities, its canonical chunks still win, but its source metadata is invalidated. That prevents hash-based sync from mistaking a partial canonical set for a complete index and forces a normal rebuild.

The original migration tests were split into `memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts`, keeping both test files below the max-lines limit without a lint suppression or loss of migration-boundary coverage.

### Root Cause

On current `main`, the same-file migration's copied-row assertion compares full row values. When canonical and legacy `meta`, `files`, `chunks`, or `embedding_cache` rows have the same key but different values, it throws a plain `Error("legacy memory <table> rows conflict with canonical memory index rows")`.

That path is reached by Memory Core schema initialization during runtime startup and by doctor before doctor enters the sidecar-import recovery block. The recovery added in #108652 catches `LegacyMemoryDerivedRowsConflictError` from the sidecar import only, so it cannot recover this plain same-file error. The result matches #108532's observed Docker behavior: startup repeatedly fails while doctor leaves the same conflict in place.

This change uses SQLite's conflict-ignore behavior only for duplicate canonical identities, then verifies identity/source ownership explicitly before dropping legacy tables. Rows that cannot be represented by the canonical STRICT schema still fail closed and retain the legacy tables.

## User Impact

Memory Core can start again when an older same-file index contains stale values for keys already present in the canonical tables. Canonical indexed content wins, safe legacy-only content remains searchable, ambiguous partial sources are marked for rebuild, and repeating schema initialization is idempotent.

Genuinely uncopyable legacy rows—for example, values rejected by canonical STRICT constraints—still hard-fail. That residual recovery case is intentionally unchanged and remains follow-up work rather than being silently discarded here.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Proof environment: Linux source checkout, Node `v25.9.0`, real on-disk `DatabaseSync` files in WAL mode. The exact current-main baseline was `cc0a977dd5b12f12d56516478f2f97a30b814c1f`; the exact patched head was `7ea8bb6b68309d073e718a5ef9a12ad26147738b`.

Each path began from an independently seeded state directory. The affected database lived at its real canonical path, `$STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. That file contained both canonical `memory_index_*` tables and partially migrated legacy `meta`, `files`, `chunks`, and `embedding_cache` tables. Every legacy table had a row with the same identity but different values from its canonical counterpart. It also had a legacy-only `LEGACY_ONLY.md` source/chunk containing the unique term `saffronquasar`, absent from canonical rows. A normal `$STATE_DIR/memory/main.sqlite` sidecar made the real startup/doctor migration path inspect the canonical target.

This reproduces the mounted-state constraint that matters to the bug: the divergent tables are inside the canonical agent database, so doctor cannot recover by renaming that database aside as a derived sidecar. No Docker daemon, container, bind mount, or OS-level rename denial was exercised; the canonical path and in-place schema state were reproduced on a normal local filesystem.

#### Current-main failure

Redacted transcript; `$PROOF_ROOT`, `$STATE_DIR`, and `$PORT` replace temporary local values.

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
cc0a977dd5b12f12d56516478f2f97a30b814c1f

$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs seed $PROOF_ROOT/main-case
{"seeded":true,"journalMode":"wal","partialMigration":true,"memoryStateHash":"9f0ed74b181898f3527a527b2f3ae8d36bd9b567439f6026e5375af45723b152"}

$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port $PORT --bind loopback --auth none
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Skipped Memory Core legacy memory index import for agent main because the sidecar could not be imported: Error: legacy memory meta rows conflict with canonical memory index rows
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
exit=1

$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
- Skipped Memory Core legacy memory index import for agent main because the sidecar could not be imported: Error: legacy memory meta rows conflict with canonical memory index rows
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0

$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs assert-baseline $PROOF_ROOT/main-case
{"baselineStillDiverged":true,"journalMode":"wal","legacyTables":["meta","files","chunks","embedding_cache"],"sidecarPresent":true,"sidecarArchived":false,"memoryStateHash":"9f0ed74b181898f3527a527b2f3ae8d36bd9b567439f6026e5375af45723b152"}

$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port $PORT --bind loopback --auth none
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
exit=1
```

Current main therefore reproduced all three reported behaviors: Gateway refused readiness, doctor exited successfully without repairing the same-file conflict, and the next Gateway invocation failed identically. The logical memory-row hash before and after doctor was unchanged.

#### Patched Gateway-first path

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
7ea8bb6b68309d073e718a5ef9a12ad26147738b

$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port $PORT --bind loopback --auth none
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
- Migrated Memory Core legacy memory index for agent main -> per-agent SQLite (1 source(s), 1 chunk(s), 1 cache row(s))
- Archived Memory Core legacy memory index sidecar -> $STATE_DIR/memory/main.sqlite.migrated
[gateway] ready

$ curl --silent --show-error --fail --write-out '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/readyz
{"ready":true,"failing":[],...}
HTTP 200

$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs assert-migrated $PROOF_ROOT/gateway-case
{"migrated":true,"canonicalWins":true,"legacyOnlyRowsRetained":true,"sameFileLegacyTablesRemovedAfterChecks":true,"ftsSentinelRows":[{"id":"legacy-only-chunk","path":"LEGACY_ONLY.md","text":"legacy-only searchable saffronquasar survives migration"}],"sidecarPresent":false,"sidecarArchived":true,"memoryStateHash":"a265a1ca48488769a16c84104a775220db89c778326a2aaa2c0603641aad1966"}

$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs memory search saffronquasar --agent main --json
{"results":[{"path":"LEGACY_ONLY.md","snippet":"legacy-only searchable saffronquasar survives migration","score":0.9695528134366842,...}]}

$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
# no Memory Core legacy-state detection, migration warning, or repair
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0

$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs assert-migrated $PROOF_ROOT/gateway-case
... "memoryStateHash":"a265a1ca48488769a16c84104a775220db89c778326a2aaa2c0603641aad1966"

$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port $PORT --bind loopback --auth none
[gateway] ready
$ curl .../readyz
{"ready":true,"failing":[],...}
HTTP 200
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs memory search saffronquasar --agent main --json
{"results":[{"path":"LEGACY_ONLY.md","snippet":"legacy-only searchable saffronquasar survives migration",...}]}
$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs assert-migrated $PROOF_ROOT/gateway-case
... "memoryStateHash":"a265a1ca48488769a16c84104a775220db89c778326a2aaa2c0603641aad1966"
```

Gateway startup repaired the same-file partial migration in place. Canonical conflicting values won, all legacy-only meta/source/chunk/cache rows survived, the actual FTS search returned the legacy-only content, all four same-file legacy tables were removed after the identity checks, and a doctor plus second Gateway/search run left the logical row state unchanged.

#### Patched doctor-first path

A separate fresh fixture proved the repair does not depend on Gateway running first.

```text
$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
- Migrated Memory Core legacy memory index for agent main -> per-agent SQLite (1 source(s), 1 chunk(s), 1 cache row(s))
- Archived Memory Core legacy memory index sidecar -> $STATE_DIR/memory/main.sqlite.migrated
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0

$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs assert-migrated $PROOF_ROOT/doctor-case
{"migrated":true,"canonicalWins":true,"legacyOnlyRowsRetained":true,"sameFileLegacyTablesRemovedAfterChecks":true,"ftsSentinelRows":[{"id":"legacy-only-chunk","path":"LEGACY_ONLY.md","text":"legacy-only searchable saffronquasar survives migration"}],"memoryStateHash":"a265a1ca48488769a16c84104a775220db89c778326a2aaa2c0603641aad1966"}

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs memory search saffronquasar --agent main --json
{"results":[{"path":"LEGACY_ONLY.md","snippet":"legacy-only searchable saffronquasar survives migration","score":0.9695528134366842,...}]}

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port $PORT --bind loopback --auth none
[gateway] ready
$ curl .../readyz
{"ready":true,"failing":[],...}
HTTP 200

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
# no Memory Core legacy-state detection, migration warning, or repair
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs memory search saffronquasar --agent main --json
{"results":[{"path":"LEGACY_ONLY.md","snippet":"legacy-only searchable saffronquasar survives migration",...}]}
$ node <proof-fixture>/fixture.mjs assert-migrated $PROOF_ROOT/doctor-case
... "memoryStateHash":"a265a1ca48488769a16c84104a775220db89c778326a2aaa2c0603641aad1966"
```

The real memory search command used the built-in FTS path (`provider: none`, vector disabled), so the searchability assertion did not depend on a mock, direct SQL-only assertion, model download, or provider credential.

### Verification

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
```

The migration tests now also cover an interrupted source with one canonical chunk and an additional legacy chunk identity. The migration keeps the canonical chunk, excludes the ambiguous legacy set, and removes the source metadata so normal hash-based sync must rebuild it.

```text
$ pnpm format packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts
$ git diff --check
$ git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
# all clean; no max-lines suppression
```

Fresh branch-mode autoreview against the rebased merge candidate found the ambiguous partial-source case above. After the source invalidation fix and focused regression test, uncommitted autoreview was rerun:

```text
$ .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.89)
```

### What was not tested

- No Docker daemon/container or real bind-mounted filesystem was used. This proof exercised the reported canonical path, WAL mode, partially migrated same-file schema, actual Gateway startup gate, actual readiness endpoint, actual `doctor --fix`, actual FTS search, and repeated-run idempotence on the local filesystem.
- Vector/semantic search was not exercised. The fixture intentionally used the credential-free FTS-only provider with vector disabled; proving a vector query would require an embedding provider/model and sqlite-vec setup. The affected migration's legacy-only content was proven searchable through the real FTS product path.
- No packaged install, full test suite, or cross-platform run was performed. The source CLI rebuilt and ran successfully on both exact SHAs; the production schema module and both touched test files have the focused verification above.
